items.title: Critical Apache Tika PDF Parser Vulnerability Allow Attackers to Access Sensitive Data
items.description: A critical security vulnerability has been discovered in Apache Tika’s PDF parser module that could enable attackers to access sensitive data and trigger malicious requests to internal systems. The flaw, designated as CVE-2025-54988, affects multiple versions of the widely used document parsing library and has been assigned a critical severity rating by security researchers. items.title: New PromptFix Attack Tricks AI Browsers to Run Malicious Hidden Prompts
items.description: A new attack vector called PromptFix exploits AI-powered browsers by embedding malicious instructions within seemingly innocent web content. The attack represents an evolution of traditional ClickFix scams, specifically designed to manipulate agentic AI systems rather than human users. items.title: Europol Says Qilin Ransomware Reward Fake
items.description: A $50,000 reward from Europol for two members of the Qilin ransomware group is a ‘scam’, according to the law enforcement agency. The post Europol Says Qilin Ransomware Reward Fake appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Microsoft Lays Out its Quantum-Safe Plans
items.description: The goal of the Quantum-Safe Program is to ensure that by 2033, all Microsoft products and services are safe by default from quantum-based attacks.
